cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: In which two forms are written exams in Roman law set?
cards.old_front: In welchen zwei Formen werden schriftliche Prüfungen im römischen Recht gestellt?
cards.back:
1. Solving a case (cf. Ch. XIV).
2. Writing an exegesis — explaining a Roman source (usually a jurist's decision) and giving reasons for it.
• Textbook note (FÜM 1 Vienna, older information): the exegesis is usually worth 28 points.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: What does a case consist of — how do you approach the solution (Ch. XIII.C)?
cards.old_front: Woraus besteht ein Fall — wie geht man bei der Lösung vor (Kap. XIII.C)?
cards.back:
Facts of the case + legal question.
1. Read the question carefully — it determines everything else (e.g. only possession, not ownership).
2. Find the relevant legal rule and state its elements.
3. Relate the elements to the concrete case.
4. Subsumption: are the requirements met? Unproblematic points briefly, problematic ones in detail.
5. Result = answer to the question.
• Proceed chronologically; where the “legal position” is asked, all positions (possession, ownership, limited rights in rem) of all parties involved.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: Which types of question are typical in property law (textbook XIII.C.2)?
cards.old_front: Welche Frage-Typen sind im Sachenrecht typisch (Lehrbuch XIII.C.2)?
cards.back:
• Acquisition/loss of possession; possession over the course of a chain of events
• Acquisition/loss of ownership; changes of ownership over time
• Position of the owner vis-à-vis a possessor or the holder of a limited right in rem
• Existence/non-existence of a pledge

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: Checklists: requirements of possession, TRADITIO, USUCAPIO (from an unauthorised person), pledge?
cards.old_front: Prüfungsschemata: Voraussetzungen von Besitz, TRADITIO, USUCAPIO (vom Nichtberechtigten), Pfandrecht?
cards.back:
• Possession: CORPUS + ANIMUS POSSIDENDI.
• TRADITIO: power of disposal (ownership/authorisation) + transfer of possession + IUSTA CAUSA.
• USUCAPIO: RES HABILIS + BONA FIDES + CAUSA + POSSESSIO + TEMPUS.
• Pledge: pledger's power of disposal + pledge agreement + claim to be secured.
• Klausur tips: before usucaption always examine derivative acquisition first; say briefly whether it is a RES MANCIPI; in case of doubt the thing is not stolen.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: How do you formulate a case solution correctly (XIII.D)?
cards.old_front: Wie formuliert man eine Falllösung richtig (XIII.D)?
cards.back:
Set out each step in complete, clear sentences so that examiners can follow the reasoning — the mere result is not enough (it could be a guess).
• Rule → application to the case → reasoning with a quotation from the facts (arg: “…”) → result.
• Do not memorise model solutions, but the structure.
• If an acquisition fails on one requirement: briefly address all requirements, then explain which one it fails on.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: Example 40 (Agatha finds a gold coin belonging to Bellona in the Forum and pockets it: “Today is my lucky day”): Does Agatha acquire possession?
cards.old_front: Beispiel 40 (Agatha findet auf dem Forum eine Goldmünze der Bellona und steckt sie ein: „Heute ist mein Glückstag“): Erwirbt Agatha Besitz?
cards.back:
Yes — immediate proprietary possession.
1. Possession = CORPUS + ANIMUS.
2. CORPUS: she pockets the coin → immediate physical control.
3. ANIMUS: arg “Today is my lucky day” — she wants to keep the coin for herself.
4. Result: acquisition of possession (according to the question, examine only possession, not ownership).

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: What is an exegesis and what is it for?
cards.old_front: Was ist eine Exegese und wozu dient sie?
cards.back:
Interpretation and explanation of a text — in Roman law usually of a Digest fragment (digest exegesis).
• Aim: to interpret a legal text and to explain a given decision and give reasons for it, applying one's knowledge of Roman law.
• Difference from case solving: there you find the solution yourself; here you explain a decision that has already been given.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.back:
1. Facts (what happened, variants?)
2. Legal question (stated expressly or inferred from the decision)
3. The jurist's decision (possibly several opinions)
4. Interpretation — the most important part.
• 1–3 concisely; infer unstated premises (e.g. if the text is about usucaption, derivative acquisition has presumably failed).
• For scholarly purposes additionally: text, translation, INSCRIPTIO, palingenesia, textual criticism.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: What belongs in the interpretation of an exegesis (XV.D)?
cards.old_front: Was gehört in die Interpretation einer Exegese (XV.D)?
cards.back:
• Which legal institution, which concepts?
• Who wants what from whom (claim)? Basis (right in rem, contract, delict)?
• Remedy (ACTIO, INTERDICTUM), standing to sue / to be sued
• Pleas, replications
• Parallel cases, controversies
• Doctrinal classification and weighing of interests
• Attitude: like a teacher making the decision plausible to a layperson — detailed, but without digressing.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: What does the INSCRIPTIO “D 20.1.29.2 Paulus libro quinto responsorum” reveal?
cards.old_front: Was verrät die INSCRIPTIO „D 20.1.29.2 Paulus libro quinto responsorum“?
cards.back: Reference: Digest book 20, title 1, fragment 29, paragraph 2; origin: book 5 of the Responsa (collection of legal opinions) of the late classical jurist Paulus.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: Model exegesis D 20.1.29.2 (Case 170): Which points of interpretation does the textbook list?
cards.old_front: Musterexegese D 20.1.29.2 (Case 170): Welche Interpretationspunkte führt das Lehrbuch an?
cards.back:
1. Legal nature of the pledge (limited right in rem, ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN REM).
2. Creation (pledger's ownership, claim — accessoriness, CONVENTIO PIGNORIS).
3. Interpretation of the agreement: “house” = house together with the land (SUPERFICIES SOLO CEDIT).
4. Not extinguished by fire — the pledge over the land continues.
5. Alienation without the creditor's consent — the pledge remains (controversy over the buyer's acquisition).
6. VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against the buyer in possession.
7. EXCEPTIO DOLI of the builder in good faith until the increase in value is reimbursed (calculation example: land 100.000, building costs 800.000, value 600.000 → 500.000).
8. MALAE FIDEI POSSESSOR: probably only IUS TOLLENDI (D 6.1.37).
9. Weighing of interests: the reimbursement does not leave the creditor worse off than if there had been no sale.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Case solving and exegesis (method)
cards.front: Model exegesis D 20.1.29.2: How much can the builder in good faith claim if the land was worth 100.000, the building cost 800.000 and the value is now 600.000?
cards.old_front: Musterexegese D 20.1.29.2: Wie viel kann der gutgläubige Bauende verlangen, wenn der Grund 100.000 wert war, der Bau 800.000 kostete und der Wert jetzt 600.000 beträgt?
cards.back:
500.000 — reimbursement only insofar as the thing has become more valuable (QUATENUS PRETIOSIOR RES FACTA EST), not the full building costs.
• Enforcement: EXCEPTIO DOLI / retention against the ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN REM.
• Africanus D 39.2.44.1 denies retention and refers to contractual claims against the seller (insolvency risk borne by the buyer).

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Controversies at a glance
cards.front: Controversies on acquisition of possession: sealing the wine barrel and wounded game — who holds which view?
cards.old_front: Kontroversen beim Besitzerwerb: Versiegeln des Weinfasses und verwundetes Wild — wer vertritt was?
cards.back:
Wine barrel (D 18.6.1.2): Trebatius — possession acquired; Labeo, Ulpian — not (only protection against substitution). (Marking timber beams, D 18.6.15(14).1: possession yes.)
Game (D 41.1.5.1): Trebatius — possession from a wounding that makes capture possible, as long as the animal is pursued; Gaius — only upon capture.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Controversies at a glance
cards.front: Controversies on acquisition of ownership by TRADITIO and usucaption: dissent about the causa; acquisition of fruits after subsequent bad faith — who holds which view?
cards.old_front: Kontroversen beim Eigentumserwerb durch TRADITIO und Ersitzung: Dissens über die Causa; Fruchterwerb bei nachträglicher Bösgläubigkeit — wer vertritt was?
cards.back:
Gift/loan dissent: Julian (D 41.1.36) — ownership passes; Ulpian (D 12.1.18 pr) — no IUSTA CAUSA, only mixing makes D owner by original acquisition, the claim for return fails because of the EXCEPTIO DOLI.
Subsequent MALA FIDES: Pomponius, Paulus — usucaption continues, acquisition of fruits no longer; Julian — both continue until the owner sues.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Controversies at a glance
cards.front: Controversies on the natural modes of acquisition: treasure, welding identical pieces of metal, SPECIFICATIO, TABULA PICTA — who holds which view?
cards.old_front: Kontroversen bei den natürlichen Erwerbsarten: Schatzfund, Verschweißen gleicher Metallstücke, SPECIFICATIO, TABULA PICTA — wer vertritt was?
cards.back:
Treasure: Sabinians — RES NULLIUS, OCCUPATIO (prevailing view); Proculians — the landowner, if aware of it, acquires already through his intention to possess; Brutus/Manilius — part of the land; Hadrian — half to the finder, half to the landowner.
Welded pieces of metal (D 41.1.27.2): Cassius — the larger/more valuable piece, or joint ownership, or the person who joined them; Proculus, Pegasus — each keeps his part.
SPECIFICATIO: Sabinians — owner of the material; Proculians — the maker; MEDIA SENTENTIA — reversible/irreversible.
TABULA PICTA: prevailing in Gaius' time — painter; Gaius, Paulus — owner of the panel.

cards.topic: 12.01. Mixed cases — Controversies at a glance
cards.front: Controversies on protection of ownership and pledge: double sale by unauthorised persons; loss after LITIS CONTESTATIO; pledge of another's thing on succession — who holds which view?
cards.old_front: Kontroversen bei Eigentumsschutz und Pfandrecht: Doppelverkauf durch Nichtberechtigte; Untergang nach LITIS CONTESTATIO; Pfand an fremder Sache bei Erbfolge — wer vertritt was?
cards.back:
Double sale (ACTIO PUBLICIANA): Neratius (D 19.1.31.2) — whoever received delivery first (even where there are two unauthorised vendors); Julian, Ulpian (D 6.2.9.4) — where there are different unauthorised vendors, whoever possesses.
Loss after LC: Proculians — liability even for CASUS (RESTITUERE); Sabinians/Paulus — only for DOLUS/CULPA.
Standing to be sued (D 6.1.9): Pegasus — possession protected by interdicts; Ulpian — FACULTAS RESTITUENDI.
Pledge of another's thing, owner becomes the pledger's heir: Paulus (D 13.7.41) — no convalescence; Modestinus (D 20.1.22) — convalescence.
Occupation of land: Labeo — immediate loss of possession; prevailing view (Ulpian) — only once the attempt at expulsion fails.
